'''Randall Dougherty''' (born 1961) is an American mathematician. Dougherty has made contributions in widely varying areas of mathematics, including [[set theory]], 
[[logic]], [[real analysis]], [[discrete mathematics]], [[computational geometry]], [[information theory]], and [[coding theory]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=DBLP: Randall Dougherty |url=http://www.informatik.uni-trier.de/~ley/db/indices/a-tree/d/Dougherty:Randall.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120404015140/http://www.informatik.uni-trier.de/~ley/db/indices/a-tree/d/Dougherty:Randall.html |archive-date=2012-04-04 |access-date=2026-02-19 |website=www.informatik.uni-trier.de}}</ref>

Dougherty is a three-time winner of the [[International Mathematical Olympiad|U.S.A. Mathematical Olympiad]] (1976, 1977, 1978) and a three-time medalist in the [[International Mathematical Olympiad]].<ref>{{IMO results |id=4 }}</ref> He is also a three-time [[William Lowell Putnam Mathematical Competition|Putnam Fellow]] (1978, 1979, 1980).<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.maa.org/awards/putnam.html |title="The Mathematical Association of America's William Lowell Putnam Competition" |access-date=2010-07-24 |archive-date=2000-02-29 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20000229230334/http://www.maa.org/awards/putnam.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>  Dougherty earned his [[Ph.D.]] in 1985 at [[University of California, Berkeley]] under the direction of [[Jack Silver]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=14967}}</ref>

With [[Matthew Foreman]] he showed that the [[Banach–Tarski paradox|Banach-Tarski decomposition]] is possible with pieces with the [[Baire property]], solving a problem of [[Edward Marczewski|Marczewski]] that remained unsolved for more than 60 years.<ref>{{Cite web |title=ALUMNEWS {{!}} Department of Mathematics |url=http://www.math.ohio-state.edu/history/math-matrix/Sp90/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110102153333/http://www.math.ohio-state.edu/history/math-matrix/Sp90/ |archive-date=2011-01-02 |access-date=2026-02-19 |website=www.math.ohio-state.edu |language=en-US}}
</ref>
With [[Chris Freiling]] and Ken Zeger, he showed that linear codes are insufficient to gain the full advantages of [[network coding]].<ref>Dougherty, Freiling, and Zeger. Insufficiency of Linear Coding in Network Information Flow.[http://code.ucsd.edu/~zeger/publications/journals/DoFrZe05-IT-Insufficiency/DoFrZe05-IT-Insufficiency.pdf] and [http://code.ucsd.edu/~zeger/publications/journals/DoFrZe05-IT-Insufficiency/DoFrZe05-IT-Insufficiency-erratum.pdf]</ref>
